title: Years and Age
summary: How old someone is, in which year something happened, and how to say one was born on a given date — the biographical uses of *metai* that ¶86 only sketched.

rules.heading: Metai Is a Plural Word
rules.statement: **Metai** (*year / years*) is a **plurale tantum**: it has no everyday singular. One year is still plural in form — *vieneri metai* (or colloquial *vieni metai*). With the special **plural numerals** used for plural-only nouns, two to nine years are *dveji / treji / ketveri / penkeri … metai*. From ten upwards the ordinary rule of ¶58 applies and *metai* stands in the **genitive**: *dešimt metų*, *dvidešimt metų*.

paradigms.caption: Counting years
paradigms.footnote: The same plural numerals appear with other plural-only nouns (*durys*, *rinkimai*). Ordinary *du metai* occurs in speech; careful style keeps *dveji metai*.

footnotes: Sources: Terje Mathiassen, *A Short Grammar of Lithuanian* (Slavica, 1996), §§ on pluralia tantum and special (plural) cardinals — *vieneri / dveji / penkeri metai*; Lithuanian school morphology of *dauginiai skaitvardžiai* (NSA / curriculum materials on the numeral); LSMU *Grammar paradigms* (medical Lithuanian) listing *penkeri metai*, *dvidešimt vieneri metai*, *dvidešimt septyneri metai*.

rules.heading: Saying How Old Someone Is
rules.statement: Age is not *I am twenty*. Lithuanian puts the person in the **dative** and states the years as the thing that ‘is’ to them: **Man (yra) dvidešimt metų** — literally *to me (there) are twenty years*. The verb *yra* is often dropped. The question is **Kiek tau / jums metų?** (*How many years to you?*). Do not say *Aš esu dvidešimt metų*.
footnotes: Sources: Mathiassen (1996), “The dative of age” (Case chapter); Ambrazas (ed.), *Lithuanian Grammar* (Baltos lankos, 1997/2006), dative experiencer constructions; LSMU medical Lithuanian paradigms: *Kiek jums metų? — Man dvidešimt penkeri. / Pacientui dvidešimt penkeri metai.* The genitive *metų* after *kiek* and after numerals from ten up is the ordinary government of ¶58, not a special ‘age genitive’.

rules.heading: In Which Year: the Instrumental
rules.statement: To answer **kada?** for a calendar year, Lithuanian uses the **instrumental plural** **metais** with an **ordinal** on the **last** element of the number only — the construction sketched in ¶86. *Gimiau tūkstantis devyni šimtai devyniasdešimt penktaisiais metais* = *I was born in 1995*. In speech the opening *tūkstantis…* is often dropped: *devyniasdešimt penktaisiais (metais)*. Writing may shorten with a figure: *1995 m.*

examples.target: Gimiau tūkstantis devyni šimtai devyniasdešimt penktaisiais metais.
Ji gimė tūkstantis devyni šimtai pirmais metais.

footnotes: Source: Mathiassen (1996), Numerals / years and dates: “To answer the question when? (*kada?*) the instrumental case is used for the year: *ji gimė tūkstantis devyni šimtai pirmais metais* ‘she was born in 1901’.” Only the last element is ordinal; earlier elements stay cardinal.

rules.heading: Full Dates: Year, Month, and Day
rules.statement: A full birth (or other) date keeps Lithuanian order **year — month — day**. The **month** is in the **genitive**; the **day** is an **accusative** ordinal (¶85). The year may be instrumental (*… metais*) or, when a month/day follows, also **genitive** (*… metų*). Example pattern: *Gimiau tūkstantis devyni šimtai devyniasdešimt penktaisiais metais kovo dvidešimtą* — *I was born on the 20th of March, 1995*.

examples.target: Gimiau tūkstantis devyni šimtai pirmais metais kovo dvidešimtą.
Ji gimė tūkstantis devyni šimtai pirmų metų kovo dvidešimtą dieną.
examples.gloss: She was born on the twentieth day of March of the year 1901.
examples.note: year in genitive when the date is fully spelled

examples.target: Šiandien tūkstantis devyni šimtai devyniasdešimt ketvirtų metų kovo dvidešimta diena.
examples.note: nominative *diena* when the date is the subject

footnotes: Source: Mathiassen (1996), same section — year instrumental or genitive when accompanied by month/day; month genitive; day accusative for ‘when?’, but nominative when the date is what ‘today is’. Order is year before date, unlike English.

rules.heading: Age, Duration, and ‘Years Ago’
rules.statement: Three neighbouring constructions must stay distinct. **Age** takes the dative person + years (*Man dvidešimt metų*). **Duration** — *for two years* — takes the **accusative of time** (¶83): *dvejus metus* / *du metus*. **Ago** uses **prieš** + accusative (¶87): *prieš penkerius metus*, *prieš metus*. **Pernai** (*last year*) and **šiemet** (*this year*) are adverbs, not case forms of *metai*.

examples.gloss: I lived in Vilnius for two years. (duration)

footnotes: Sources: Mathiassen (1996) on accusative of duration with plural numerals (*ji prabuvo dvejus metus Vilniuje*) and on *prieš* + accusative; ¶83 and ¶87 of this course; *pernai* / *šiemet* as lexical time adverbs in standard descriptions and dictionaries (DLKT / school vocabularies).

vocabulary.notes: With metai: vieneri metai. Feminine vienerios.

drills.explanation: Age question: *Kiek tau metų?*
Dative of age: *Man dvidešimt metų*, not nominative *aš*.
Plural numeral with plurale tantum *metai*: *penkeri metai*.
From ten up, *metai* → genitive *metų*: *dešimt metų*.
*Aš esu … metų* is the English-shaped error. Questions and dative statements are fine.
Last element ordinal + instrumental plural *metais*: *penktaisiais metais*.
Month in the genitive before the day: *kovo dvidešimtą*.

drills.stem: Match the job of *metai* in each sentence — which labels are right?
drills.explanation: *1995 metais* answers *when?* (calendar year), not how old someone is.

drills.stem: In **tūkstantis devyni šimtai devyniasdešimt penktaisiais metais**, how many words before *metais* are **ordinals**?
drills.explanation: Only *penktaisiais* — the last element.

drills.stem: Complete: **______ baigiau mokyklą.** (Last year I finished school.)
drills.explanation: *Pernai* = last year. *Šiemet* is this year; *prieš metus* would be ‘a year ago’.

drills.stem: Complete: **Prieš ______ atvažiavau.** (I arrived five years ago.)
drills.explanation: *Prieš* + accusative: *penkerius metus*. Instrumental *metais* is for calendar years.
Year before month/day. English month-first order inside the Lithuanian phrase is wrong.
Last element *one* with *metai* → *vieneri metai*: *dvidešimt vieneri metai*.

drills.stem: How many **different** time constructions appear in **Man dvidešimt metų, gyvenau ten dvejus metus, o prieš metus grįžau**?
drills.explanation: Age (*man … metų*), duration (*dvejus metus*), ago (*prieš metus*).

drills.title: Apie Rūtą
drills.passage: Rūtai dabar dvidešimt penkeri metai. Ji gimė tūkstantis devyni šimtai devyniasdešimt devintaisiais metais birželio dešimtą. Penkerius metus ji gyveno Kaune, o prieš trejus metus atvažiavo į Vilnių. Pernai baigė mokyklą; šiemet studijuoja. — Kiek tau metų? — klausia draugė. — Man dvidešimt penkeri, — atsako Rūta.
drills.translation: Rūta is now twenty-five. She was born on the tenth of June, 1999. She lived in Kaunas for five years, and three years ago she came to Vilnius. Last year she finished school; this year she is studying. "How old are you?" asks a friend. "I am twenty-five," answers Rūta.

options: dative of age + plural numeral with *metai*
questions.explanation: Person in the dative; years with *penkeri metai* because the last element is 2–9.

questions.stem: In the birth date, *birželio dešimtą* is:
questions.explanation: Month genitive, day accusative ordinal — Mathiassen’s full-date pattern.

questions.stem: Which time readings in the passage are correct?
questions.explanation: The instrumental year is when she was born, not how old she is.

questions.stem: How many times does a **dative** person of age appear (*Rūtai* / *Man* / *tau*)?

drills.explanation: Dative *jums* in the age question.
*Šiemet* = this year.
*Dešimt* forces genitive *metų*, not nominative *metai*.

drills.stem: Why is ***Aš esu penkeri metai*** wrong?
options: Age needs a dative person: *Man penkeri metai*
Because age must use the instrumental *metais*
Because *yra* is forbidden in age sentences
drills.explanation: Mathiassen’s dative of age — the experiencer is dative, not nominative.

drills.stem: Complete: **Gyvenau ten ______.** (I lived there for two years.)
drills.explanation: Duration = accusative: *dvejus metus* (Mathiassen).

drills.stem: Complete: **Gimiau ______.** Which can answer *when were you born?* with a year?
drills.explanation: Calendar year (*metais*), spelled year, or *ago* can situate birth in time. *Man trisdešimt metų* states present age, not the birth year.

drills.stem: Complete: **______ pradėsiu darbą.** (Next year I shall start work.)
drills.explanation: *Kitąmet* = next year.

drills.stem: In **Kiek jums metų?**, how many words stand in the **genitive**?
drills.explanation: Only *metų* — *kiek* takes the genitive. *Jums* is dative.

drills.stem: Complete: **Du tūkstančiai ______ grįšiu.** (I shall return in 2030.)
drills.explanation: Last element ordinal instrumental plural: *trisdešimtaisiais metais*.

options: It is a plurale tantum in ordinary use
Age puts the person in the dative
*Aš esu … metai* is the standard age formula
drills.explanation: The fourth is the interference error this section exists to kill.
